```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(targets)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
source("src/R/scrna-seq_utilities.R")   # list utilities_r in this report's quarto_report() line
source("tools/R/provenance.R")
out <- report_dir()   # artifacts/ next to the HTML: save figures/tables here (emptied each render)

theme_set(theme_bw(base_size = 11))
tar_load(colors_vec)                    # cell-type colours from the config (plotting: colours:)
compartments <- c("Stroma", "HSC", "MNC")
condition_levels <- c("WT", "Het mCh−", "Het mCh+")
```

<!-- LOADING RULES
     - Read targets by their literal name: tar_read(x) / tar_load(x). The pipeline scans for these to
       link the report to its inputs; tar_read_raw(paste0(...)) is invisible to it, so the report
       would not re-render when that input changes.
     - Prefer small extract targets (data frames: metadata, UMAP coordinates, counts of a few genes)
       to whole Seurat objects. If a Seurat object is needed: load → extract → rm() + gc().
     - Parameters: tar_load(qc_params) / tar_load(proc_params), never hard-coded numbers or paths.
     - Chunk options that depend on data: #| eval: !expr isTRUE(get0("FLAG")) — a bare !expr FLAG
       breaks the pipeline's dependency scan, which runs before the report's own code. -->

```{r}
#| label: load
# TEMPLATE: one small target per compartment, read by name
meta <- list(
  Stroma = tar_read(<target_stroma>),
  HSC    = tar_read(<target_hsc>),
  MNC    = tar_read(<target_mnc>)
) |>
  bind_rows(.id = "compartment") |>
  mutate(compartment = factor(compartment, levels = compartments))
```

# Data

<!-- What goes in: which cells (after QC? which sort fractions?), how many per sample, and anything
     unusual about them. A table the reader can check numbers against. -->

```{r}
#| label: cell-counts
meta |>
  count(compartment, sample.name, name = "cells") |>
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, options = list(dom = "t", pageLength = 20))
```

# <Result 1 — a heading that states the finding, e.g. "mCh+ HSCs shift towards the MK branch">

<!-- One section per result. Pattern: a sentence on what the figure shows → the figure (with a
     caption) → a paragraph on what it means and what it does NOT show (caveats, alternatives). -->

<What this figure shows and how to read it.>

```{r}
#| label: fig-result-1
#| fig-cap: "<Caption: what is plotted, what each point/colour is. Shown as the lightbox title.>"
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 4
p <- ggplot(meta, aes(<x>, <y>, colour = <group>)) +
  geom_point(size = 0.3) +
  facet_wrap(~ compartment, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL)
ggsave(file.path(out, "result-1.png"), p, width = 10, height = 4, dpi = 300)   # for slides / sharing
p
```

<Interpretation. Refer to the figure as @fig-result-1. Give the numbers, not just the direction.>

## Per compartment

<!-- Repeated plots for several compartments/samples go in tabs, not one under another. -->

::: {.panel-tabset}

```{r}
#| label: per-compartment
#| output: asis
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 5
for (cmp in compartments) {
  cat("### ", cmp, "\n\n", sep = "")
  print(
    ggplot(filter(meta, compartment == cmp), aes(<x>, <y>)) +
      geom_point(size = 0.3) +
      labs(title = cmp)
  )
  cat("\n\n")
}
```

:::

## Table

<!-- Tables: searchable DT for anything over ~10 rows; round numbers; name columns in words. -->

```{r}
#| label: tbl-result-1
result_tbl <- meta |>
  group_by(compartment, sample.name) |>
  summarise(cells = n(), .groups = "drop")
write.csv(result_tbl, file.path(out, "result-1.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
DT::datatable(result_tbl, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
              caption = "<What each row is.>")
```
